To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lung function reference values are transcendent functions of body height, body mass, age and sex, and are not linear functions of age.
the development of lung function is a transcendent function that depends on age, body height, mass and gender.

the dependent variables, i. e. lung function parameters, are expressed as a single transcendent function of the independent variables, age, height and mass, and that the parameters are expressed as a function of the logarithms of the three independent variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of reference values for lung function variables in healthy subjects and the modelling of lung function as a transcendent of age, body mass and height.
the development of reference values for lung function in healthy subjects.
the development of lung function in children and young adults, with the aim of providing reference values for clinical practice and for the interpretation of epidemiologic studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented lung function reference values and normal ranges are more accurate and reliable than the previous ones and that the new approach of modelling lung function development as transcendent functions is superior to the conventional approach of using age, body height or body mass as independent variables.
the presented lung function reference values are the most accurate and reliable reference values for healthy subjects of all ages and both sexes.
the new reference values are superior to all previously published values in terms of accuracy and reliability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lung function reference values should be based on a model that takes into account age, body height, body mass and possibly other factors.

we have presented a model of lung function development which is based on a large number of healthy subjects, that it is valid for the age range 6-81 yr, that it is applicable in clinical practice, and that it allows the calculation of individualized reference limits.
the new reference equations for the lung function variables are superior in accuracy to the existing equations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reference values are based on a large population of normal subjects and that the reference values reflect the normal development of lung function in healthy subjects.
a transcendent function is a more accurate description of lung function than a simple polynomial function of age and height.
the reference values and normal ranges should be age-, height- and mass-specific, and that the use of age- or height-specific reference values should be abandoned.
